grammar.title: so...that与such...that
grammar.explanation: so + 形容词/副词 + that从句；such + (a/an) + 形容词 + 名词 + that从句。so强调程度，such强调性质。
grammar.structure: so + adj./adv. + that; such + (a/an) + adj. + n. + that

examples.sentence: The film was so boring that I fell asleep.
examples.translation: 电影太无聊了，我睡着了。

examples.sentence: It was such a boring film that I fell asleep.
examples.translation: 这是如此无聊的电影，我睡着了。

grammar.ieltsTip: 雅思写作中so/such...that结构可增强表达的感染力，让论述更生动。

questions: How have family structures changed in your country?
What role do grandparents play in modern families?
Is it better for children to grow up in large or small families?
How will family relationships change in the future?
speaking.sampleAnswer: Family structures in China have undergone significant transformations, shifting from extended multi-generational households to smaller nuclear families, particularly in urban areas where housing constraints and career demands prevail. Grandparents still play vital roles, often serving as primary caregivers for grandchildren while parents work, though this arrangement can sometimes generate intergenerational conflicts over child-rearing philosophies. Whether large or small families are preferable depends on context: large families offer richer social support and diverse role models, while small families can provide more individualized attention and resources per child. Looking ahead, I expect family relationships will become more diverse and flexible, with rising acceptance of single-parent families, blended families, and child-free couples. The fundamental function of families—providing love, support, and belonging—will endure, even as their forms multiply.
speaking.tips: 家庭话题常用对比和趋势分析。
